title: Corroboration-Based Interviewing Training Services for USCIS Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate (FDNS)
description: The Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate (FDNS), has a requirement for Corroboration-Based Interviewing (CBI�) Training Services. USCIS anticipates awarding a purchase order for eight (8) customized, three-day, in-person training courses during the period of performance. Each course shall support up to twenty-four (24) FDNS participants. The required training shall be tailored to the USCIS FDNS investigative, screening, fraud detection, national security, and adjudicative support environment. The training shall provide evidence-based instruction and practical application in investigative interviewing methods, including interview planning and strategy, cooperation building, credibility assessment, evidence disclosure, questioning strategies, information management, communication, memory, and techniques for eliciting reliable information. Course content shall include, at a minimum, interviewer mindset and demeanor, proactive versus reactive interviewing, productive and unproductive questions, topic funnels, cooperation assessment concepts, trust-building, effective introductions, social dynamics, communication, credibility assessment, myths about detecting deception, limitations of non-verbal cues, verbal indicators, cognitive approaches to detecting deception, stages of memory, memory errors, evidence disclosure planning, evidence framing, strategic opportunities to further the interview, and strategies for mitigating uncooperative behavior. The training shall include instructor-led demonstrations, scenario-based activities, frequent practical exercises, and individualized participant feedback. The contractor shall provide qualified instructors with experience in investigative interviewing, evidence-based interviewing methods, law enforcement investigations, workplace investigations, legal psychology, or related fields. The anticipated instructional model includes three (3) in-person instructors and one (1) virtual instructor, or an equivalent instructional staffing model approved by USCIS FDNS. Training will be delivered at USCIS-designated locations, which may include USCIS Headquarters, USCIS field locations, USCIS training facilities, or other Government-approved locations. Final training dates and locations will be coordinated after award between the Contracting Officer�s Representative and contractor personnel. USCIS will provide or coordinate access to training facilities. Anticipated facility needs include one main lecture room, three smaller breakout rooms, audiovisual capability, and internet access if required for instruction or virtual instructor participation. The contractor shall provide all course materials necessary to conduct the training and coordinate with USCIS FDNS regarding training dates, locations, participant rosters, facility requirements, and logistics. Post-training case consultation or coaching may be included if provided as part of the contractor�s standard course package.

description: Amendment 1 (25 Aug 26) Updates: "Presolicitation" This MACH1_AOI opportunity is updated with the following changes: 1. All submissions must adhere to the procedures and guidelines outlined in the parent MACH1 framework document unless otherwise tailored herein. Any resulting agreement will be an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) executed under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS) is seeking innovative commercial design and engineering partners to develop a comprehensive, site-specific design package for rapidly deployable Earth-Covered Munitions (ECM) storage facilities at Dyess AFB, Texas. The Government requires rapidly deployable Class V munitions storage facilities to support evolving global threats and warfighter readiness. Traditional MILCON processes and standard ECM build face structural and procedural bottlenecks�ranging from slow curing times to complex bespoke formwork�that prevent rapid deployment. This AOI seeks architectural and engineering innovations that bypass these traditional bottlenecks. The Government is looking for design concepts incorporating advanced formwork, rapid-curing materials, modular structural arches, or other commercial methodologies that accelerate the timeline while fully maintaining all required blast resistance, structural integrity, and environmental controls. There are (2) two lines of effort (LOEs) for this requirement: LOE 1 - Design & Planning (Design) and LOE 2 - Physical Construction. description: Amendment 2 is being issued to publish answsers to questions and to provide additioanl campus maps and extend the deadline for the submission of qutoes. Amendment 1 is being issued to publish campus wide maps and to extend the deadline for questions and the deadline for the submission of quotes. The goal of this project is to remove and replace the existing public address system across the entire Robert J. Dole VA Medical Center campus. This new system will replace all the components of the public address system. This includes the design, removal of the existing systems, procurement of new equipment, installation, programming, testing, and training to ensure fully functional public address systems at the end of the contract. The new public address system will be a modern design, fully monitored system capable of decentralized zone control, message storage, and self-health monitoring. The system design must include speaker line verification and message delivery verification. The project will replace the existing fiber backbone for the public address system and will not connect to the existing enterprise network. The system must include all relevant safety and regulatory standards. Removal of Existing System: Carefully remove all existing system components, including speakers, microphones, wiring, and control units. The system must be removed and installed in phases to minimize system outages. Ensure safe and efficient disposal or recycling of old equipment according to relevant environmental and safety regulations. Procurement of New Equipment: Procure all necessary components for the new public address system, which may include speakers, desktop paging microphones, amplifiers, end-of-line monitoring devices, control units, and message servers. The equipment shall meet all standards for medical and public safety applications. The public address systems shall be Biamp�s Vocia or equivalent. The equipment and proposed layout shall be reviewed by the Medical Center for comment and approval prior to purchase on behalf of the government. If documents are not approved, revisions will be required before approval. The contractor shall provide floor plans with proposed locations for all the equipment. The Medical Center will provide the initial floor plans to the contractor. Installation of New System: New Speakers Speakers are to be installed throughout the corridors and common areas of each building, approximately every 25 feet, ensuring optimal sound coverage. Establish headend locations in each building to decentralize electronic control, simplifying installation, troubleshooting, and maintenance. Treat each floor of the buildings as individual zones to prevent issues in one area from affecting others, and provide flexibility for further zoning with additional amplifier channels. Install and connect the active end-of-line monitoring devices to monitor and report on the health of the speakers and wiring. Wiring and Cabling: Install all necessary wiring and low-voltage cabling for the new system, ensuring adherence to electrical codes and standards. Label and document all wiring and connections for ease of future maintenance and troubleshooting. System Programming and Integration: Program the new public address system, configuring zones and message priorities according to the site's needs. Integrate the system with any existing building management systems, fire alarm systems, nurse call system, or other safety and emergency systems as required. Testing and Quality Assurance: Perform rigorous testing of the entire system to verify functionality, sound quality, and reliability. Conduct end-to-end tests to ensure that messages are delivered accurately and the system self-health monitoring features are operational. User Training and Documentation: Provide comprehensive training for facility staff, including manufacturer certification, user-level training, installation training, and administrator-level training for the new public address system. Supply detailed user manuals, system schematics, and maintenance documentation. Final Inspection and Handover: Conduct a final inspection of the installed system in each building to ensure compliance with project specifications and quality standards. Rectify any deficiencies or issues identified during the final inspection. Obtain official sign-off from project stakeholders to confirm satisfactory completion of the project. The contractor will provide a complete commissioning of the system. Ongoing Support and Maintenance: Offer a 2-year service period from the date of completion of the project. Equipment warranty as provided by the original equipment manufacturer. Evaluating Factors: The following factors will be considered when evaluating the contractor(s) proposals: Bidding contractors shall be of good standing in with past performance for the government. Bidding contractors shall have local service providers to support services needs in the future. The service support should be within 1-hour drive of the Robert J. Dole Medical Center. Five-year manufacturer warranty on all equipment. Certified seller and installer by the original equipment manufacturer. The contractor is responsible for delivering fully functional turnkey solution. By the end of the contract�s period of performance, each of the buildings on campus will have a fully operational public address system. Period of Performance: 180 calendar days after Notice to Proceed The contractor is responsible for delivering fully functional turnkey solution. By the end of the contract�s period of performance, each of the buildings on campus will have a fully operational public address system. On-site Performance: Delivery and Installation dates shall be pre-scheduled with the COR. description: CONSTRUCTION STATEMENT OF WORK Date: September 13, 2025 Project Number: 556-24-113 Project Name: Oil Transformer and Switch Enclosure Upgrade (GC) Location: Captain James A. Lovell FHCC 3001 Green Bay Rd, North Chicago, IL 60064 Part 1: Project Scope of Work Overview: Contractor shall provide all tools, materials, labor, quality assurance, and supervision for renovations resulting in a complete, compliant, and fully-functional project. Replace medium voltage oil-filled transformers that serve the following buildings on the James A. Lovell FHCC campus: 1, 3, 9, 11, 66, 137 and 187. Transformers have 4160 volt primary and 208/120 volt secondary. There are (4) transformers rated for 150 KVA, (2) transformers rated for 300 KVA and (1) transformer rated for 750 KVA. title: 12905B24SS1174122 � Sources Sought for Dry Bean Winter Nursery USDA-ARS East Lansing MI
description: This is a Sources Sought notice Only. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. This Sources Sought is issued for information and planning purposes only as part of USDA ARS market research and does not itself constitute an RFQ. This requirement is covered under NAICS code 111421 with a small business size of $3.2M. Responses may suggest alternative NAICS for considers. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of qualified sources; Small Businesses; HUBZone small business; service-disabled, veteran-owned small business; 8(a) small business; veteran-owned small business; woman-owned small business; or small disadvantaged businesses; Responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. Procure a winter nursery in Puerto Rico to support the ARS Sugar Beet and Bean Research Unit (SBRU), East Lansing, MI dry bean breeding program. The winter nursery is used to advance breeding materials by a generation over the winter, which greatly speeds up breeding progress. Bean seeds from an estimated 500 to 800 entries will be shipped from East Lansing to Puerto Rico in September 2026 for planting in the winter nursery. Seed must be planted by December 2026. Seeds from each entry should be planted in 10 ft rows. Bean plants must be well-maintained during the growing season with sufficient water, fertilizer, and weed management to produce a healthy crop. Seed should be bulk harvested via row and shipped back to East Lansing, MI by April 2027. The Government does not intend to make an award based on responses to this inquiry. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. Capability Statement All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. Business concerns that possess the capabilities necessary to undertake this work should submit complete documentation of their capabilities to the Contracting Officer. Capability statements shall include the Contractors contact point to discuss their response. The capability statement should include: 1) Acknowledgement that they are able to provide the subject supplies/services being requested; 2) Interested vendors should identify their size standards in accordance with the Small Business Administration; 3) At least three previous requirements that are similar to the requirement include a discussion of the Contract type, delivery method, duration, etc.; 4) Any other information considered relevant to this requirement; and 5) The government requests that no proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in the response. Any vendor responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine their qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. After review of the responses received, a combined synopsis/solicitation may be published on sam.gov depending on the responses received. All responses to this Sources Sought Notice must be received by the notice�s POC by the deadline in order to be considered. Responses may not be returned. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this Inquiry. Do not submit pricing information in response to this Request.

title: DLA Energy Fuel Transportation Services - Progreso, Yucat�n, Mexico (JP5)
description: 1. Notice Type This Sources Sought Notice is issued for market-research and planning purposes only. It does not constitute an Invitation for Bids (IFB), Request for Proposals (RFP), Request for Quotations (RFQ), solicitation, or commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. Responses to this notice will not be considered offers, proposals, or quotations, and no award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. 2. Agency and Purpose The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is conducting market research to identify responsible commercial sources capable of providing fuel transportation, cross-border customs support, delivery, and offload services in support of U.S. Navy maritime operations in the vicinity of the Yucat�n Peninsula, Mexico. The anticipated support is for Southern Border operations in the vicinity of the Gulf of America. 3. Anticipated Requirement The Government anticipates a requirement for the contractor to furnish and deliver approximately 20,000 U.S. gallons of JP-5 from DFSP Houston to Progreso, Yucat�n, Mexico, per delivery event. For market-research purposes, respondents should identify their ability to support recurring deliveries at the stated quantity and provide recommended delivery lead times. The method of transportation is not prescribed. Respondents may propose the commercial transportation method or combination of methods that most effectively, safely, lawfully, and reliably supports the mission, including tanker truck, ISO container, or another commercially available approach. 4. Commercial Delivery and Acceptance Concept The Government is seeking commercial solutions under which: The contractor shall provide transportation services for Government-owned fuel and perform all activities necessary to deliver and offload the fuel at the designated delivery point in Progreso, Mexico. The Government will accept the full delivered quantity during each delivery event. The fuel will be offloaded directly into a Navy vessel, as directed by the Government representative. The contractor shall provide all transportation, coordination, personnel, equipment, documentation, and services necessary to safely complete delivery and offload. Detailed fuel-quality, inspection, quantity-verification, acceptance, safety, environmental, and operational requirements will be established in the performance work statement (PWS) or solicitation. 5. Required Contractor Capabilities Interested parties shall have the ability to provide the following: Bulk transportation of JP-5 or comparable aviation/marine petroleum products via tanker truck, ISO container, or other suitable commercial transport capacity. Transportation from a Defense Fuel Support Point (DFSP) to Progreso, Mexico. Cross-border transportation operations between the United States and Mexico. Ability to properly coordinate delivery of fuel products the Port of Progreso and other applicable ports, terminals, piers, and local authorities. In-transit security and accountability for fuel from pickup through Government acceptance. All equipment required to transfer fuel at destination, including compatible hoses, couplings, pumps, grounding/bonding equipment, spill-response equipment, and calibrated/certified quantity-measurement equipment, as applicable. Ability to conduct fuel offload to shore-side receiving equipment and/or directly into a Navy vessel, as directed. Contingency and recovery procedures for transportation disruption, border delays, weather, equipment failure, fuel-quality discrepancies, or unsuccessful delivery/offload. 6. Requested Capability Statement Content Interested parties are requested to submit a capability statement that addresses the following: Company information Legal business name. Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code, if applicable. Point of contact, title, business telephone number, and business email address. Relevant experience Describe recent and relevant examples of fuel transportation support, cross-border petroleum logistics, port delivery, or vessel offload support. Include the fuel type, approximate quantity, transportation method, general origin/destination region, period of performance, and scope of customs/port/offload support. Proposed commercial approach Identify proposed transportation method(s). Describe how the company would support delivery to Progreso, Mexico and perform direct-to-vessel offload. Identify estimated delivery lead time after order placement. Cross-border and port capabilities Briefly identify any relevant licenses, permits, certifications, or established commercial arrangements your company holds that are necessary to execute the proposed approach. 7. Response Instructions Submit responses no later than September 9, 2026; 11:00 am Eastern Standard Time Email: DDFBunkers@dla.mil Subject Line: Sources Sought Response � Fuel Transportation Services to Progreso, Mexico Questions regarding this Sources Sought Notice shall be submitted in writing to the above Bunkers email address. 8. Additional Information This notice is intended to support market research, acquisition planning, and the Government�s determination of an appropriate acquisition approach. The Government may use the information received to assess commercial availability, small-business capability, risk, delivery feasibility, and the appropriate scope for a future solicitation. The Government may revise the requirement, issue a solicitation, elect not to issue a solicitation, or pursue another acquisition approach.

title: MACH1_AOI_Muns_Igloos at Dyess AFB - LOE 1 and LOE 2
description: This Area of Interest (AOI) is published under the Modernized Agile Construction Horizons (MACH1) Umbrella Program Notice. All submissions must adhere to the procedures and guidelines outlined in the parent MACH1 framework document unless otherwise tailored herein. Any resulting agreement will be an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) executed under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS) is seeking innovative commercial design and engineering partners to develop a comprehensive, site-specific design package for rapidly deployable Earth-Covered Munitions (ECM) storage facilities at Dyess AFB, Texas. The Government requires rapidly deployable Class V munitions storage facilities to support evolving global threats and warfighter readiness. Traditional MILCON processes and standard ECM build face structural and procedural bottlenecks�ranging from slow curing times to complex bespoke formwork�that prevent rapid deployment. This AOI seeks architectural and engineering innovations that bypass these traditional bottlenecks. The Government is looking for design concepts incorporating advanced formwork, rapid-curing materials, modular structural arches, or other commercial methodologies that accelerate the timeline while fully maintaining all required blast resistance, structural integrity, and environmental controls. There are (2) two lines of effort (LOEs) for this requirement: LOE 1 - Design & Planning (Design) and LOE 2 - Physical Construction. See attachment PDF: MACH1_AOI_FA890326OT003_Muns_Igloos_Dyess_ 21 Aug 26.pdf

title: Automated Armory Tracking System
description: The Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune Contracting Office is soliciting quotes from qualified contractors to deliver an Automated Armory Tracking System (AATS) for the Camp Lejeune Provost Marshal�s Office (PMO). This solicitation is for a contract to establish a secure, web-based Software as a Service (SaaS) subscription for a modernized armory tracking system. The system is intended to streamline operations, maintain accurate custody tracking of assets, and ensure strict compliance with Marine Corps inventory standards. Key Requirements and Scope: Contract Type: A firm-fixed-price contract for commercial services. Contract Period: One (1) 12-month base period with two (2) subsequent 12-month option periods. Scope: Provide a turnkey AATS solution delivered as a web-based SaaS platform. The scope includes software licensing, secure cloud setup, data migration, personnel training, and continuous technical support as specified in CLINs 0001 through 2001. The system must be FedRAMP Moderate or High authorized and support real-time asset tracking, digital check-in/check-out, and automated receipt generation. Evaluation Factors: Quotes will be evaluated based on Price, Technical Capability, and Past Performance. This is a Competitively Sourced procurement set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) under NAICS code 513210. All specific details are contained within the Request for Quotation (RFQ) and PWS.

title: Germany – Construction work – Teil-GU Wunstorf TGA
description: Die KRH Psychiatrie Wunstorf, bestehend aus Erwachsenenpsychiatrie, Kinder- und Jugendpsychiatrie sowie Maßregelvollzug, hat auf der gesamten Liegenschaft Bedarf an baulichen Erneuerungs- und Erweiterungsmaßnahmen festgestellt. Für die Erwachsenenpsychiatrie hat eine Zielplanung 2019 ergeben, dass der Bedarf eines Stationsneubaus mit 6 Stationen besteht. Als Baufeld wurde ein Bereich im Norden der Liegenschaft gewählt, in dem aktuell ein Mitarbeiterparkplatz sowie das Sozialzentrum bestehen. Diese Nutzungen werden verlagert. Für das Projekt wurde ein Antrag auf Förderung nach § 9.1 KHG eingereicht und genehmigt. Der Neubau besteht aus: - dem Neubau eines Stationsgebäudes der Erwachsenenpsychiatrie (H2) mit sechs Stationen à 19 Betten zuzüglich 2 Aufstellreserven und 4 Plätzen der Tagesklinik, - dem Ersatzneubau Sozialzentrum (H1) mit Cafeteria und Mehrzwecksaal, - der dezentralen Kompensation des entfallenden Mitarbeiterparkplatzes mit aktuell 47 Stellplätzen in drei verschiedenen Parkplatzen auf der Liegenschaft, - sowie der Umstrukturierung der angrenzenden Freianlagen und Verkehrsflächen.

description: IDA Ireland is seeking to establish of a Single Party Framework for the Design, Delivery and Management of IDA Ireland’s Property Management System on the Salesforce platform. Justification for the maximum 7 years Framework length - The successful candidate may be required to undertake potentially significant upfront time investment in further discovery, detailed solution design, data migration, configuration, testing, integration and organisational change activities. title: EKFB JV - Waste Management Services
description: Eiffage Kier Ferrovial BAM (EKFB) JV is seeking expressions of interest from interested parties for Waste Management Services to support the delivery of the C23 project, which forms part of the HS2 Main Works Civils Contracts. The C23 project consists of three delivery areas; North Chilterns to Aylesbury (NC2A), Calvert to Greatworth (C2G), and Greatworth to Southam (G2S). EKFB JV intends to run a procurement exercise to select a preferred supplier/s on a framework agreement basis with a call off mechanism. EKFB JV may look to award multiple frameworks to suit geographical capability dependant on the response to this EOI. EKFB JV is proud to have been appointed by HS2 to deliver civil engineering works across an 80km section of the new high speed rail link between the Chiltern Tunnel and Long Itchington Wood. Our scope of the works includes 15 viaducts, 6.9km of green tunnels, 22km of road diversions, 81 bridges and around 30 million cubic metres of excavation.

title: The Supply of MAMMUT PRO 2.0 3L HOODED JACKET
description: Unite Procurement UK Limited (part of Unite Holding SE), on behalf of the Ministry of Defence, is seeking suppliers to join the Unite Procurement Platform to support the procurement of Mammut Pro 2.0 3L Hooded Jackets. Requirement Overview The current stock of Mountain Equipment (ME) Makalu student winter jackets received through procurement in 2025 are not fit for purpose for winter training delivery. The jacket is more suited to summer delivery and requires replacement prior to winter delivery this year. To ensure suitable student jackets are available for winter delivery in the future, the currently held ME jackets will be replaced with a more appropriate alternative identified through subject matter expert guidance. The existing ME Makalu jackets will be repurposed to support summer delivery courses, thereby extending equipment longevity through seasonal rotation. The Mammut Pro 2.0 3L Hooded Jacket was proposed by the supplier and has been verified by subject matter experts as highly suitable for the requirement. The Mammut Pro 2.0 3L Hooded Jacket offers: Excellent suitability for winter training delivery Availability at the full quantity required Availability in fire red colour to maintain student fleet identification Competitive value for money Gore-Tex protection and durability for demanding training environments The existing ME Makalu jackets will transition to summer delivery support at both training locations, optimising the equipment fleet through seasonal use. The Unite Procurement Platform (Unite | Simplify indirect procurement with our smarter platform) offers a compliant route to market for UK Public Sector organisations to manage low-value, high-volume procurement. How to Apply Interested suppliers should register their interest by contacting Unite Procurement UK Limited and provide details of their product range, modification capabilities, and maintenance services. Further information on the onboarding process for the Unite Procurement Platform will be provided upon expression of interest and can also be found at the link attached. Unite Procurement UK Limited does not intend to appoint a sole supplier for this requirement. Instead, multiple suppliers may be onboarded to the Unite Procurement Platform to ensure a diverse and competitive supply base, supporting flexibility and choice for the Ministry of Defence and associated organisations. Suppliers are encouraged to express their interest by the stated closing date to ensure early consideration. However, applications to join the Unite Procurement Platform will be welcome at any time beyond the initial deadline. Unite Procurement UK Limited reserves the right to review and onboard new suppliers on a rolling basis to meet evolving requirements and to maintain a dynamic and responsive supplier network. Contact For any enquiries and interest, please email defence.support@unite.eu with the subject title 'TSS 787 Opportunity'

title: Harry S Truman Streetscape Perimeter Construction Project
description: The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS) New England Region, Acquisition Management Division intends to hire a construction contractor to implement and enhance security and esthetics for the area around the Harry S Truman (HST) Streetscape Construction building located in Washington DC. The project originated in response to the events of 9/11 where high-profile government buildings were targeted by terrorists. This major renovation project will replace the temporary security measures surrounding the building to provide countermeasures that will secure the building, protect employees and visitors, and improve the surrounding streetscape by creating an attractive and accessible environment for pedestrians. Once complete, the temporary security measures will be replaced with tested and proven countermeasures that will secure the building, protect employees and visitors, and improve the surrounding streetscape by creating an attractive and accessible environment for pedestrians. The project involves civil/site construction of approximately 162,000 square feet of streetscape (sidewalks, curb & gutter, utilities, etc.), requiring 4 phases for completion. title: Bobcat S150 Skid Steers Repair - Sources Sought
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE INTRODUCTION: The Mission Installation Contracting Command (MICC) � Fort Bliss, TX is issuing this sources sought nottice as a mean of conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of performing manufacturer?level repairs on four (4) Bobcat S150 Skid Steers. Information received will support the Government�s acquisition planning. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided regarding submitted material DISCLAIMER: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A �REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP)� TO BE SUBMITTED. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. RESPPONSES WILL NOT BE RETURNED TO THE RESPONDER. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) OR RFP, IF ANY ISSUED. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: Overview: The contractor shall restore four (4) inoperable Bobcat S150 Skid Steers located at Fort Bliss, TX. Restoration includes repairing the electrical system, completing scheduled maintenance, repairing the cab, repairing the fuel system, replacing all tires, replacing the operator seat, repairing the Bob?Tach system, and testing each machine to verify proper operation. Basic Services: The contractor shall provide the appropriate number of personnel to come to Fort Bliss to complete restoration of the four (4) Bobcat S150 Skid Steers. Electrical System: The contractor shall complete full replacement of the main, cab, and ancillary working harness, and ignition switches. Mechanical System: The contractor shall complete the replacement of the drive belts, all filters (air, fuel, hydraulic, oil), and fluids. Cab & Safety: The contractor shall complete the repair of the full cab frame, door kit, installation of new operator seats, new wiper kits, and lighting. Mobility: The contractor shall complete the replacement with new solid flex tires across the fleet. Fuel System: The contractor shall complete the repair or replacement of fuel sensors and water cooler tanks. Bob?Tach System & Final Testing: The contractor shall repair the Bob?Tach system and test each machine to verify proper operation after all repairs and replacements are completed. ** Additional details are provided in the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS), Attachment 1.** - Organizations capable of performing these services are requested to submit: Company Information Organization name, address, website, email, telephone number, business size, and type of ownership. - Capability Statement: A tailored statement demonstrating the ability to meet the requirements, including documentation supporting organizational and staff qualifications. If subcontracting or teaming is anticipated, describe the proposed structure and management approach. The Government will use this information to assess market capacity to provide services consistent with the scope and scale of this requirement. ELIGIBILITY: The applicable NAICS code is 811310. The PSC is J024. All business sizes are encouraged to respond; however, respondents must clearly identify their business size in their capability statement ADDITIONAL INFORMATION AND SUBMISSION DETAILS (CAPABILITIES STATEMENT) A Performance Work Statement (PWS) is included as Attachment 1. The anticipated contract type is Firm Fixed Price. Responses shall be submitted by e-mail in Microsoft Word or PDF format to nancine.a.dezir.mil@army.mil and matthew.l.altenberg.mil@army.mil no later than 10:00 AM MDT on 9 September 2026. Include the synopsis number in the email subject line and on all submitted documents. Do not submit classified material. The Government is not obligated to pay for information provided, and no claims shall arise from responding to this notice.

title: Ground Station as a Service
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE (SSN) ONLY This Sources Sought Notice is for market research purposes in identifying capable small and large business vendors and does not constitute a Request for Proposal or Quotation. It is not considered to be a commitment by the Government to award a contract nor will the Government pay for any information provided; no basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result from a response to this Sources Sought Notice or Government use of any information provided. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. The information provided in this SSN is subject to change and does not bind the Government to any future obligations. All submissions become the property of the Government and will not be returned. Any information that a respondent considers proprietary and/or copyright should be clearly marked as such. OVERVIEW Requirement: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information System (NESDIS), Office of Satellite and Mission Operations (OSPO) requires an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for Ground Station as a Service (GSaaS) including site certification, telemetry downlink data services, and satellite commanding data services. This will satisfy NESDIS current requirements for commercial remote telemetry-only downlink for partner missions, Constellation Observing System for Meteorology Ionosphere and Climate-2 (COSMIC-2), Korea Multi-Purpose Satellite�5 (KOMPSAT-5), and PAZ. The GSaaS contract will provide agility for NESDIS to add or reduce ground station service task orders for future NESDIS or partner missions as they are defined. Under this contract, the contractor is responsible for operating ground status sites that meet strict geographical, technical, and regulatory requirements, including securing necessary radio frequency licenses. The contractor shall provide ancillary engineering support services, such as systems compatibility assessments and proficiency testing, while strictly complying with physical security programs, cybersecurity frameworks like NIST or ISO, and government data rights that restrict the external distribution of sensitive information without explicit permission. NAICS Code/Size Standard: The applicable NAICS code is 517810 All Other Telecommunications, and the business size standard is $40 million. Key Criteria: Site Requirement � The Contractor shall propose and operate GSaaS at sites that meet the technical specifications for satellite to ground communications and security, that meet mission geographical requirements, and that have availability to meet the Government�s anticipated tasking schedule. Scheduling Requirement � The Contractor shall accept Government service requests according to the scheduling interface agreements in the task order. Service Requirement � The Contractor shall meet the technical performance standard that 95% of scheduled contacts are attempted, successfully completed, that the Eb/N0 margin is greater than 3 dB, and that data are delivered to the specified NOAA internet point of presence within 60 seconds of the end of the contact. Security Requirement � The Contractor shall provide artifacts that demonstrate that sites and services meet security requirements according to the security frameworks established by the Contractor and approved by the Government. Regulatory Requirement � The Contractor shall be solely responsible for local and OPPA Ground Station as a Service (GSaaS) IDIQ Performance Work Statement international regulatory compliance related to occupancy and operation of the service sites and for providing the services from those sites. The contractor shall secure, maintain, and comply with radio frequency licenses for the services provided. Required Response Information: Capable small business vendors are requested to provide the following information in response to this SSN announcement: Company Name/Division, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone number, and website URL (if available). A single Point-of-Contact name, title, telephone number, and e-mail address. Unique Entity ID (UEI). Please note that companies must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be considered potential sources (beta.SAM.gov). Business Size in relation to NAICS 541715 and any SBA socio-economic certifications. Demonstrated capabilities in meeting the needs of the Key Criteria listed above. Conflict of Interest: Please detail the extent to which the respondent is aware of any potential organizational conflict of interest issues related to this requirement. Response Format: In order to better assist in the review of responses to this SSN, respondents are encouraged to prepare a capabilities statement that does not exceed 5 pages. Response Submission Requirements and Deadline: Responses to this SSN should be submitted via e-mail attachments, received no later than 12:00 PM, ET, 9 September 2026 to: Contracting Officer: Trang Tran at Tran.Tran@noaa.gov; and Contracting Specialist: Markita Simmonds at markita.simmonds@noaa.gov.

description: See RFQ Document and SOW within for complete Description. Title of project: Trauma and Crime Scene Clean Up Contract - Cleveland, OH and surrounding area. Purpose of the project: VA Northeast Ohio Health Care system is looking to procure as needed services for Trauma/Crime scene Clean-up when needed for the entire health care system. Contract vehicle will be a firm-fixed price IDIQ. Background: Following a suicide, violent death, or severe accident, the removal of biohazardous materials, such as blood, human remains (tissue and bone fragments), and other contaminants, must occur on varied surfaces. The clean-up and decontamination of these locations is called trauma scene clean-up (also referred to as crime scene clean-up*). These are general terms used to describe the cleaning of blood, human remains, or any biohazardous material following an incident that results in environmental contamination.

description: SPECIAL NOTICE Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract Notice Type: Special Notice / Notice of Intent to Award Sole Source Agency: Department of the Treasury Bureau: Bureau of Engraving and Printing (BEP) Title: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Maintenance Services Description This is a Notice of Intent to award a sole source Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract and is not a Request for Quotations (RFQ) or Request for Proposals (RFP). Under the authority of FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services will Satisfy Agency Requirements, the Department of the Treasury, Bureau of Engraving and Printing (BEP), intends to award a sole source Firm-Fixed-Price contract to: Protec Surface Technologies S.R.L. Via Benaco 88 Bedizzole, Bhs 25081, Italy The anticipated contract will consist of one (1) Base Year and four (4) one-year Option Periods. Services will be performed at the following BEP facilities: Washington Currency Facility (DCF), Washington, DC Western Currency Facility (WCF), Fort Worth, TX The contractor shall provide preventive maintenance, calibration, inspections, diagnostics, troubleshooting, emergency repair services, technical support for BEP-owned Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) systems. Services shall be performed in accordance with the manufacturer's recommended maintenance procedures to ensure continued operational reliability, equipment performance, and system availability. Based on market research, the Government has determined that Protec Surface Technologies S.R.L. is the only known source capable of providing these services. The PVD systems require proprietary equipment, software, diagnostics, maintenance procedures, and technical expertise unique to the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). The Government is unaware of any other source capable of performing these services while maintaining the required operational integrity of the equipment. Responses This notice is not a solicitation. However, any responsible source that believes it can meet the Government's requirement may submit information demonstrating its capability to provide the required services. At a minimum, the response shall demonstrate that the source is authorized by Protec Surface Technologies S.R.L. to service the IPC 1100 PVD machines and has authorized access to the proprietary software, diagnostics, technical data, maintenance procedures, and other OEM-controlled resources necessary to perform the required services without voiding the manufacturer's warranty. Responses shall be submitted electronically to: Contracting Officer: Lasonia Brown Email: lasonia.brown@treasury.gov; lasonia.brown@bep.gov To ensure timely receipt, responses shall be submitted to both email addresses. Vendor inquiries regarding this notice may be directed to the Contracting Officer at the email addresses provided above. Responses must be received no later than 12:00 Noon, EDT, September 9, 2026. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. If no responsible sources submit information sufficient to demonstrate the capability to meet the Government's requirement, the Government intends to proceed with a sole source award to Protec Surface Technologies S.R.L. **See Attached Justification For Other Than Full and Open Competition: JOFOC_2031ZA26Q00136_PVDMaintenance_pdf

description: Shaft & Prop Repair on 2 Coast Guard boats at USCG Base Boston located at 427 Commercial St, Boston, MA. 02109 Introduction The United States Coast Guard is issuing this Open Market Request for Quote (RFQ) to establish an award in support of the Statement of Work (SOW). This procurement is being conducted pursuant to FAR 19.5.01 as a small business set-aside. The associated NAICS code for this procurement is 332710, which has a small business size standard of 500 employees. Questions pertaining to this solicitation must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer at peter.psanis@uscg.mil no later than 5pm EST on September 04, 2026. The subject line of the email must include the solicitation number (RFQ No.70Z02426Q0000324). Each question should identify the solicitation section, page number, paragraph number, or other identifier relating to the question. Questions without this information may or may not be answered. Site visit is highly recommended and can be coordinated through: curtis.d.lefever@uscg.mil (857) 416-3376 Quote Submission Instructions Quote submissions are due by 12:00pm EST on September 9th, 2026 and must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer, peter.psanis@uscg.mil Evaluation: Factor 1 � Technical Experience Vendor must provide evidence of required experience as indicated in the SOW. Evaluation: Factor 2 � Relevant Experience It is highly desirable that offerors include relavent experience related to the SOW. The information provided in the Relevant Experience submission must be sufficiently detailed so that the Government can determine whether the project(s) demonstrate relevant experience of similar scope, size, and complexity of this acquisition. Evaluation: Factor 3 � Price The Government will evaluate the Offeror�s price quote for completeness, accuracy, compliance, and to determine price reasonableness. Basis of Award: This procurement is being conducted pursuant to FAR 19.5.01 as a small business set-aside. The Government intends to award a single firm-fixed price task order to the Offeror whose quote represents the best value to the Government. Comparative evaluations (comparing quotes to each other) will be used to select the Offeror that is best suited and provides the best value based on the following three (3) factors in descending order of importance: Factor 1 - Technical Experience, Factor 2 - Relevant Experience, and Factor 3 - Price. The Government will use the tradeoff process to make a determination of best value. This means that the Government will consider issuing an award to other than the lowest priced Offeror, other than the highest technically and relevant experience evaluated Offeror based on an assessment and tradeoff between non-price factors (Factor 1 and 2) and price (Factor 3). The non-price factors are more important than price. However, the closer the quote�s non-price evaluations are to one another, the more significant the price factor becomes in determining the best value to the Government. This is only a request for quotation. No guarantee of award is made or implied. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation, either before or after the closing date.

title: Optical Fiber Cables
description: This is a Notice of Proposed Contract Action under the FAR Part 12 Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. Notice is for information only; a solicitation will not be issued. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION. No contract will be awarded on the basis of offers received in response to this notice. The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 334413 with a small business size standard of 1,000 employees. The Government intends to negotiate a sole source contract with Coastal Connections, 2085 Sperry AVE STE A-B, Ventura, CA 93003-7452. The specific brand name or equal requirements include: End-Cap Cable (P-FAnskFUnsk-10/230/3-15.24), Qty 1 Fiber Type: LMA-PM-10 Fiber Connectors: FC/APC to FC/UPC (Narrow Key, Slow Axis Alignment) Details: Collapsed Core 50-100um Long (Both Ends), 3mm OD Tubing, 15.24�15.44m Long Performance: PER 18dB @ 1060nm; NA @ 850nm @ D4Sigma: TBD ID: Red boots (angle polish); Red/Blue bands (UPC polish) Note: Cables >10m may have splices in tubing; fiber remains continuous. End-Cap Cable (P-FAnskFUnsk-10/230/3-30.48), Qty 1 Fiber Type: LMA-PM-10 Fiber Connectors: FC/APC to FC/UPC (Narrow Key, Slow Axis Alignment) Details: Collapsed Core 50-100um Long (Both Ends), 3mm OD Tubing, 30.48�30.68m Long Performance: PER 18dB @ 1060nm; NA @ 850nm @ D4Sigma: TBD ID: Red boots (angle polish); Red/Blue bands (UPC polish) Note: Cables >10m may have splices in tubing; fiber remains continuous. Single Mode PM Cable (493 nm), Qty 2 Fiber Type: Corning 480 nm PM Fiber Connectors: FC/APC to FC/APC (Narrow Key, Slow Axis Aligned) Details: 3mm OD Jacket, 150�151 Meters Long Performance: Insertion Loss (IL) near 5.7 dB or less Single Mode PM Cable (650 nm), Qty 2 Fiber Type: Corning 630 nm PM Fiber Connectors: FC/APC to FC/APC (Narrow Key, Slow Axis Aligned) Details: 3mm OD Jacket, 150�151 Meters Long Performance: Insertion Loss (IL) near 2.7 dB or less The required optical fibers are intended to be incorporated into existing laboratory setups which are currently using Coastal Connections branded fiber optic cables. To ensure compatibility, functionality, and interchangeability with the existing infrastructure and cabling, it is imperative that any additional cables be of the exact same brand as those currently in place. The introduction of an alternate brand of cable into the existing laboratory setup has the potential to result in performance degradation of the system. This would require extensive troubleshooting by skilled personnel to mitigate issues, thereby unacceptably reducing operational efficiency. Based on these strict compatibility requirements, the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with Coastal Connections as the only known source capable of meeting this requirement. This is a notice of proposed contract action and not a request for competitive proposals; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement or proposal, which shall be considered by the agency. All inquiries should be sent by email to jennifer.calandra@us.af.mil. Responses must be submitted by the date/time listed on the notice. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government in future procurements. Responses received will be evaluated; however a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government anticipates an award date on or before 25 September 2026. A Sole Source Justification will be attached to the subsequent Notice of Award in accordance with applicable regulation.

description: Amendment A00004 (9/2/2026): The purpose of this amendment is to provide responses to industry questions, incorporate additional terms and conditions, and extend the due date and time for submission of quotes. Industry Questions and Government Responses: Question #1: On-Site Presence for Administrative Meetings: The SOW designates the "Contractor" as the lead for Phase I Site Surveys and the Phase III Final Site Inspection (Deliverable 6). If our firm utilizes a highly qualified local subcontractor for physical installation, will the TSA permit our designated Prime Contract Project Manager to attend these meetings virtually, or is the physical, on-site presence of the Prime Contractor's administrative representative required? Government Response: The Prime Contractor remains responsible for all contract performance. Virtual attendance by the Prime�s Project Manager is permitted provide a qualified on-site representative is physically present for the site survey, installation coordination, and final inspection. The Government reserves the right to require in-person attendance if needed at a date and time that is mutually agreeable to the parties. Question #2: County Insurance Filing: SOW Section VIII states that the Contractor must have approved insurance on file with Milwaukee County. Will the airport authority accept the Prime's insurance file if it is supported by our local subcontractor�s active municipal policies naming Peractos LLC and Milwaukee County as additional insureds? Government Response: The Contractor must meet all insurance requirements in the SOW and any Milwaukee County or airport authority requirements. Subcontractor insurance may support the filing if it meets the required coverage and additional insured requirements, but it does not relieve the Prime Contractor of responsibility. Final acceptance of insurance documentation is subject to Milwaukee County/airport authority approval. Question #3: Defensive Berm & HESCO Technical Specifications: SOW Section III requires a 10-foot-high (13-foot on one side), 3-foot-thick horseshoe-shaped dirt berm utilizing "HESCO style or similar defensive barriers" filled with compacted imported dirt. To support accurate material takeoff and shipping pricing, could the Government provide the total linear footage or perimeter footprint dimensions of the required horseshoe configuration? Additionally, are there specific technical model numbers required for the HESCO barriers, or any structural compaction density tests required for the fill dirt? Government Response: Quoters should base their quote on the SOW requirements and any observations and/or measurements taken during the optional site visit. The Government cannot provide the total linear footage or perimeter dimensions for the horseshoe configuration. Please include the total linear footage and perimeter dimensions as part of the high-level design plan in your Factor 1 - Draft Project Plan response. No specific HESCO model number is required. Any �HESCO style or similar� product must meet the required height, thickness, configuration, and stability requirements. Compaction testing is not required. Question #4: Electrical Infrastructure Specifications: SOW Section III (Phase II - Electrical Requirements) specifies running electrical lines approximately 180 feet from the canine kennel to a new utility pole, and subsequently to the magazine. Could the Government provide the electrical parameters (voltage, phase, and amperage) of the power source at the canine kennel? Additionally, are the utility pole, exterior lighting fixture, and conduit to be entirely contractor-procured, or is any of this equipment being provided as Government-Furnished Property (GFP)? Government Response: The Government will not provide Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) / Government Furnished Property (GFP). Quotes must include all materials, equipment, labor, and installation necessary to complete the electrical work in accordance with the SOW. The Contractor must verify existing electrical conditions during the comprehensive site survey in Phase 1 - Design. Question #5: Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14): We note that the solicitation is a Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS 238990. However, FAR Clause 52.219-14 is not listed among the filled-in clauses under FAR 52.212-5. Could you please confirm if the Limitations on Subcontracting clause is applicable to this requirement? If so, does the standard 25% self-performance requirement for specialty trade contractors apply, or is subcontracting up to 100% of the on-site installation labor permissible? Government Response: FAR Clause 52.219-14 �Limitations on Subcontracting� (Oct 2022) does not apply as this requirement is being set aside for Total Small Business and the contract amount is not expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold. Question #6: Wage Determination Standards (SCA vs. DBA Construction Rates): SOW Section III details on-site civil works, concrete post embedment, and structural barrier installation. However, Attachment 2 incorporates a Service Contract Act (SCA) Wage Determination (No. 2015-4899) rather than a Davis-Bacon Act (DBA) construction wage determination. Could the Government please confirm if all on-site physical construction labor is to be mapped strictly to the provided SCA classifications, or if a DBA Wage Determination will be issued for the construction/installation portion of the work? Government Response: The Government has reviewed the applicable labor standards requirements and will amend the solicitation to incorporate Attachment 5 - Davis-Bacon Act WD # WI20260001 for the installation portion of the requirement. The Davis-Bacon Act wage determination applies to laborers and mechanics performing physical installation work at the site, including fence installation, post embedment, gate and barbed wire installation, defensive barrier/berm installation, fill placement and compaction, electrical installation, site restoration, and related punch list work. Attachment 2 - Wage Determination No. 2015-4899 applies to covered service employees performing separable non-construction support services, including administrative coordination, project documentation, permit support, meeting minutes, and closeout documentation. Quoters are responsible for properly classifying employees and complying with all applicable wage determinations incorporated into the solicitation. Question #7: Contract Documents, Statement of Work, Section III, Phase II � Electrical Requirements. Please advise if electrical feed of +- 180�-0 can be run overhead? Government Response: Quoters may include an overhead electrical run as part of their high-level design plan. Any overhead electrical work is subject to Government review and approval, airport authority requirements, applicable electrical codes, and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) notification/determination requirements under 14 CFR Part 77, including submission of FAA Form 7460-1 if required. Question #8: Contract Documents, Statement of Work, Part B. Technical Requirements, Phase I Design. Please advise if required comprehensive site survey and preliminary design drawings need to be prepared by a registered Wisconsin engineer? Government Response: Not required. Question #9: Contract Documents, Statement of Work, Part B. Technical Requirements, Phase I Design. description: *Questions and Answers posted as an Attachment 9/4/2026 The Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) intends to award a Purchase Order to provide post-accident toxicological testing of human samples, tox box program management, and related scientific services for the Office of Railroad Safety, Drug and Alcohol Division (RRS-25) to meet the requirements described in the Statement of Work (SOW). This requirement supports the FRA by providing scientifically sound and legally defensible toxicological analyses of urine, whole blood, and tissue samples, obtained from railroad and railroad contractor employees in post- accident testing and 49 CFR Part 219/Part 40 compliance review services to ensure continuing public confidence in the forensic integrity and scientific credibility of the FRA Post-Accident Toxicological Testing (PATT) Program. The quotations will be provided to Government Officials for the purpose of assuring that the Quoter has a complete understanding of the scope of this effort and has the capability to provide a complete solution to the Statement of Work (SOW). Any quotation that is incomplete or non-compliant with any requested submission requirement of this RFQ may immediately be removed from further consideration. Quotes failing to include required laboratory credentials or qualified key personnel may be immediately removed from consideration. Contractors must maintain one or more of the following: Certification by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services/Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (DHHS/SAMSHA) National Laboratory Certification Program (NLCP) Accreditation as a forensic toxicology laboratory by the American Board of Forensic Toxicology (ABFT), or whomever ABFT employs as a credentialling body for its accreditation (currently it is the ANSI National Accreditation Board (ANAB) with an additional ABFT checklist). Accreditation as a forensic toxicology laboratory by the College of American Pathologists (CAP) It is the Government�s intent to award a small-business set-aside purchase order to the responsible Quoter whose quotation, in conforming to the RFQ, provides the overall best-value to the Government. The total estimated value of this purchase order is estimated at $2,600,000.00. The Government reserves the right to cancel this RFQ without award if the needs of the requirement are not met. This RFQ does not commit the Government to pay for the preparation and submission of a quotation. The Government has assigned the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 541380 � Testing Laboratories for this procurement. The Product and Service Code (PSC) for this requirement is B529 � �Special Studies/Analysis: Scientific Data.� *See File titled "Synopsis Solicitation" for the full document.

title: Request for Information - Wide-Area IR Persistent Surveillance System
description: This Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS)/Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational purposes and market research only; it does not constitute a solicitation. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for any expenses associated with preparing/submitting information in response to this posting. The information provided may be used by the Government in developing its acquisition strategy, statement of work/statement of objectives, and/or performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained within their response as instructed later in this posting. The United States (US) Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance & Special Operations Forces (ISR & SOF) Directorate, Special Warfare (SW) Program Office (AFLCMC/WISN) is conducting market research to identify possible sources capable of providing Wide Area Infrared Surveillance (WAIS) System. REQUIREMENT Key Performance Parameters (KPPs) 1. Performance & Detection Capabilities � Passive Operation: Provide self-protection and situational awareness without emitting detectable signals. � Detection & Tracking Capacity: Automatically detect and classify up to 100 simultaneous thermal signatures within 1 second. � Detection Ranges: Capable of long-range acquisition across multiple target profiles: � Commercial aircraft up to 93 miles (at 12,000 ft altitude). � Group 2 Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) up to 10 miles. � Personnel and ground vehicles up to 5 miles. � Personnel detection minimum range is 500 meters. � Tracking Accuracy & Reliability: Achieve a 90% overall detection probability. Target tracking accuracy must maintain �3 degrees at 10 miles and �5 degrees at 93 miles (evaluated at a 95% confidence level). � Field of View (FOV): The entire system, comprised of multiple sensors, shall provide a minimum of 360� horizontal and 125� vertical hemispherical coverage. � Individual sensors shall have a minimum FOV of 90 degrees. � AI & Automation: Utilize advanced AI/ML-driven algorithms for automated target detection, classification (e.g., distinguishing small drones from commercial airliners), predictive analysis, and pattern recognition. 2. Integration & Interoperability � C2 Integration: Incorporate an open-architecture design to integrate seamlessly with Command and Control (C2) systems, existing Tactical Grid infrastructure, and TACP mission software/hardware. � Sensor Fusion: Capable of fusing multiple passive IR data streams (from within the IRIS-P system), and fusing with active radar and other external EO/IR sensors to deliver comprehensive, multi-domain situational awareness. � Communication Standards: Utilize common tactical interface standards (e.g., MIL-STD-6016) to interface natively with broader electromagnetic spectrum awareness systems. 3. System Operations & Data Management � Usability: Operable by a single user with minimal training. Features a user-friendly laptop workstation interface providing real-time data, tracking options, and automated alerts accessible within 3 seconds of a request. � Operator Verification: Support robust "operator-in-the-loop" workflows to verify, refine, and override automated threat detections. � Networking & Throughput: Process high-fidelity thermal imaging data at a minimum of 1 Gbps throughput on a hard-wired, closed network. Supports real-time data streaming, efficient data compression, and on-demand retrieval. � Security & Storage: Implement role-based and security-clearance-based access control for stored data. Support Unencrypted, Type 3, and Type 1 communication pathways (Type-1 encryption specifically required for sensor data in transit). � Data storage shall be scalable to accommodate increasing data volumes. 4. Physical Characteristics (SWaP) & Environmental Durability � Deployability: Modular, low Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP) footprint. Deployable in rugged environments across mobile (dismounted, vehicle-mounted) and stationary (tripods, fixed towers) configurations. Minimize time and effort required to relocate stationary configuration. � Environmental Ruggedization: Must meet MIL-STD-810G standards. Fully operational in extreme temperatures (-30�C to 55�C) and adverse weather conditions (rain, fog, snow). Please see attachment for additional information regarding this requirement and instructions on responding to this Request for Information.

title: Amendment 1: Solicitation- WT 18058173 Airfield and Weather Flight Carpet Replacement
description: This project entails the removal and replacement of flooring approximately 4,370 square foot of carpet on the first floor of Building 122, Peterson Space Force Base (PSFB). The contractor will coordinate with the 21st Civil Engineering Squadron (21 CES) to conduct bio-environmental screening for hazardous materials beneath the existing flooring. Once cleared, the contractor will remove the old carpet and rubber cove base, managing daily site clean-up and off-base debris disposal, as on-site equipment storage is strictly prohibited. To prepare the space, the contractor will relocate standard furniture --coordinating with the Government to ensure all IT cables, power cords, and personal items are removed beforehand. The installation phase requires laying new, commercial-grade modular carpet tiles or planks directly over the existing vinyl flooring using low-VOC adhesives. The contractor will also install a new vinyl cove base, trim door bottoms for proper clearance, and perform any necessary wall spackling and painting to repair damage caused during the removal of the old baseboards. The project will conclude with the repositioning of all furniture and a final Quality Assurance acceptance inspection conducted by 21 CES Operations Flight personnel. Please see attached Combo Solicitation and attachments for detailed information required.

title: RFI/Sources Sought for "Planning and Execution of the MHSRS for the DHA in Support of the ASW(HA)
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/SOURCES SOUGHT (SS) NOTIFICIATION TO INCLUDE INDUSTRY FEEDBACK 1. Title: Planning and Execution of the Military Health System Research Symposium (MHSRS) Support Services for the Defense Health Agency (DHA) in Support of the Assistant Secretary of War - Health Affairs (ASW(HA)) 2. Contracting Office: Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity, Research and Development Contracting Division 1 - Contracts Branch 4 3. Contracting Office Location: Fort Detrick - Frederick, Maryland 4. Summary: This RFI/SS is issued solely for information and planning purposes and shall not be construed as a solicitation, restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach, or serve as an obligation on the part of the DHA. In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Revolutionary FAR Overhaul 15.101(c)(2), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are advised that the United States Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI/SS. All costs associated with responding to this RFI/SS will be solely at the interested responder�s expense. Not responding to this RFI/SS does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposal, if any are issued. No evaluation letters and/or results will be issued to responders responding to this RFI/SS. The information resulting from this RFI/SS will determine interest and capabilities available in the marketplace; and will assist in developing acquisition strategy. 5. Background/Scope: The ASW(HA) is the principal advisor to the Secretary of War and the Under Secretary of War for Personnel and Readiness for all Department of War and force health protection policies, programs, and activities. In carrying out these responsibilities, the ASW(HA) exercises authority, direction, and control through the DHA. The ASW(HA) plays a critical role in research by overseeing, directing, and allocating resources for military-specific medical research, including Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs and the Defense Health Program funded research. A strategic research focus of ASW(HA) is areas that impact military operations � specifically medical care during deployed operations. The DHA on behalf of the ASW(HA) requires knowledge management and symposium support services for the execution of the MHSRS. This meeting serves as an annual forum to report the results of federally funded medical research supporting the deployed warfighter. The MHSRS aligns with the ASW(HA)�s role as the overseer of health policy and the DHA�s mission as a joint, integrated Combat Support Agency enabling the U.S. Army, Navy, and Air Force medical services to provide a medically ready force to Combatant Commands. This requirement is for non-personal support services to fully support the ASW(HA) with symposium planning and execution of the annual MHSRS. The Contractor shall provide support for all planning, execution, and post-event activities for the annual MHSRS at a no cost basis as the Contractor will recover all costs in the form of revenue from attendee registration fees, sponsorships, and exhibitor fees. It is the intent of the MHSRS to create a symposium environment that encourages maximum participation from Government and private industries that support the ASW(HA) and the DHA in any of their mission requirements. The MHSRS shall be designed to promote an exchange of information, display market products and innovations, as well as set a routine expectation that stabilizes the communication between industry and Government. The NAICS for this requirement is 561920. The anticipated contract type is a no cost contract. How to Respond to this RFI/SS: Please submit a Capability Statement that describes relevant experience, expertise, and capabilities based upon the size and scope of this requirement as outlined in the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS). Each response should include the following business information and must not be more than ten (10) pages in length: a) Company name, mailing address, email address, telephone, website address (if available), and the name, telephone number, and email address of a point of contact having the authority and knowledge to clarify responses with Government representatives. b) Unique Entity ID number, CAGE Code, and company structure (Corporation, LLC, partnership, joint venture, etc.). Companies must also be registered in the System for Award Management at www.sam.gov to be considered as potential sources. c) Small Business representation and corresponding NAICS. Are you a small business under NAICS 561920? Are you an 8(a)?Are you a small business under any other socio-economic category? d) Any and all Government Contracts/IDIQs (e.g. Federal Supply Schedule, OASIS, etc.) currently held (to include the vehicle and your contract number) that could be used to fulfill this requirement. e) Description of the company�s specific and relevant experience and expertise to fulfill this requirement. Experience must be of similar size and scope. Please provide examples or provide references of previously completed deliverables related to this requirement. Does your company have experience in planning and executing scientific research meetings with scientific abstract submissions, peer review of abstracts, and schedule build for speakers? Does your company have experience with no cost contracts? f) Provide information relating to capabilities, novel ideas, and industry best practices. Industry capabilities need to meet the needs of the Government�s requirements as outlined in the draft PWS. Do not regurgitate the draft PWS tasks, rather, outline company specific capabilities that match the work outlined in the draft PWS in order for the Government to make a fair capabilities determination. Requested (but not required nor evaluated): Any industry feedback to the attached draft PWS. Capability statements will be reviewed/evaluated for (1) Relevant experience based on the size and scope of the outlined requirement; (2) Company specific capabilities that match the work outlined in the draft PWS. title: Harry S Truman Streetscape Perimeter Construction Project
description: The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS) New England Region, Acquisition Management Division intends to hire a construction contractor to implement and enhance security and esthetics for the area around the Harry S Truman (HST) Streetscape Construction building located in Washington DC. The project originated in response to the events of 9/11 where high-profile government buildings were targeted by terrorists. This major renovation project will replace the temporary security measures surrounding the building to provide countermeasures that will secure the building, protect employees and visitors, and improve the surrounding streetscape by creating an attractive and accessible environment for pedestrians. Once complete, the temporary security measures will be replaced with tested and proven countermeasures that will secure the building, protect employees and visitors, and improve the surrounding streetscape by creating an attractive and accessible environment for pedestrians. The project involves civil/site construction of approximately 162,000 square feet of streetscape (sidewalks, curb & gutter, utilities, etc.), requiring 4 phases for completion. description: The National Library of Medicine (NLM) requires a license and maintenance agreement for its existing docWizz� Pro Plus Imaging Software, which supports NLM�s ongoing digitization and long-term preservation of historical medical print materials. title: CONTROL UNIT
description: The Government intends to award a sole source procurement under RFO 12.102(a) to Span-America Medical Systems, Inc., or an authorized offeror providing the product of the approved source. The Dayton VA Medical Center (VAMC) has a requirement for ten each new Control Unit (Span-America P/N 27686). The high-performance digital pump is required to activate the active therapeutic modes of the Custom Care Convertible Low Air Loss (LAL) series mattresses used by the Dayton VAMC. By connecting this unit to the mattress system, it provides consistent Low Air Loss (LAL) and alternating pressure therapies to treat Stage I-IV pressure injuries. This particular model is necessary to use the mattresses with the Umano bed frames currently in use by the Dayton VAMC. This contract action is for supplies for which the Government is soliciting only one source BRAND NAME ONLY under the authority of RFO 12.102(a). The determination not to compete this requirement is within the discretion of the Government. title: Cable Television and Broadband Internet Services for FRCSW
description: The Commander Fleet Readiness Centers (COMFRC) Procurement Group, Patuxent River, MD 20670 hereby gives notice of their intent to award a purchase order to Cox California Telcom, L.L.C., 5159 Federal Blvd, San Diego, CA 92105 (CAGE Code: 66AT6) on a Sole Source basis in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 13.106-1(b)(1)(i), as only one source is reasonably available to satisfy agency requirements. The requirement is for commercial subscription television and broadband telecommunications services to support daily administrative, informational, and operational continuity functions across Fleet Readiness Center Southwest (FRCSW) facilities. Services encompass multi-channel informational broadcast distribution to maintain situational awareness, dedicated data connectivity to support specialized auxiliary communication services (such as American Sign Language video telecommunication), and network connectivity to ensure uninterrupted business and financial operations. Cox Communications is the incumbent authorized cable service provider and maintains the sole existing cable infrastructure currently servicing the required buildings at Fleet Readiness Center Southwest (FRCSW). The significant capital expenditure required to establish a parallel infrastructure from an alternative vendor makes any other source commercially unfeasible for this requirement. The proposed contract action is for supplies or services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b). THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. All responsible sources may submit a response via email beginning September 3, 2026, 12:00 PM EST, through September 9, 2026, 12:00 PM EST Points of contact for this requirement are Kelsey Herbert, kelsey.l.herbert2.civ@us.navy.mil and Tiffany Crayle, tiffany.l.crayle.civ@us.navy.mil
